instructions.value: During sad-image trials, participants either viewed without explicitly regulating, accepted the emotion by noticing thoughts and feelings and allowing them to remain without pushing them away, or reappraised the image by reinterpreting it to reduce its negative impact. Participants practiced the strategies with an experimenter before scanning.

stimuli.value: Sad and neutral photographs, including sad images from the International Affective Picture System and a normed set of sad and neutral images used in prior MDD imaging studies.

spans.text: Task images were drawn from two sources: (i) sad images from the International Affective Picture System based on normative sadness ratings ( Mikels et al. , 2005 ) and (ii) a normed set of sad and neutral images used in previous MDD imaging studies ( Wang et al. , 2005 , 2008 ; Dichter et al. , 2009 , 2010 ).

value: Post-trial affect ratings on a visual analog scale ranging from 1 (most negative) to 4 (most positive); ratings were analyzed across view, accept, and reappraise conditions.
